documents.text: Cognitive behavioral therapy for insomnia, called CBT-I, is the first line treatment for chronic insomnia. It combines sleep restriction, stimulus control and thoughts about sleep. Patient contact: 619-555-0142, MRN: 00123456.

Burnout at work shows up as exhaustion, cynicism and reduced effectiveness. Manager check-ins, workload changes and time off are common first steps. Mindfulness practice can support recovery but does not replace changing the workload.

Panic attacks peak within minutes and then fade. Breathing exercises and gradual exposure therapy reduce their frequency. Anxiety that returns after a panic attack is common and treatable with therapy.

Sleep hygiene means a regular wake time, a dark cool room and no screens before bed. Good sleep habits help with insomnia and with depression, but they work best alongside therapy when symptoms are strong.
